content: True dispassion (*Vairagya*) is turning away from all transient pleasures as one turns away from poison.
author: Adi Shankara
explanation:
In the uncompromising architecture of Advaita Vedanta, Adi Shankara reveals that non-dual consciousness is the eternal reality behind all fleeting phenomena.

This teaching (True dispassion (*Vairagya*) is turning away from all transi...) focuses directly on true and dispassion. When we clear away reactive illusions and anchor ourselves in timeless principles, the mind recovers its pristine clarity and inner resilience.

True realization is never an abstract intellectual debate—it is an active discipline lived through quiet integrity and conscious presence in everyday moments.
practicalInsight: Apply this teaching on true today: take a deliberate pause before reacting, align your actions with quiet integrity, and refuse to let transient friction disturb your center.
reflectionPrompt: How can you embody deeper true and dispassion in the primary challenge you are navigating right now?
